Subject: GPU runway huddle: Acme pipeline & reserve asks

Hi team —

I pulled the March-close pipeline and attached a quick snapshot (tabbed by close week + expected QPS). Acme is now showing two possible close windows: pilot (May 15 start) and production (Aug commit). They’re asking for a recommended reserved slot plan + burst budget for the pilot.

Ask: can infra + finance give a recommended reserve profile for pilot vs prod by EOD tomorrow so we can align to sales/CS asks? I’ve looped Sarah so procurement visibility is present.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme_pipeline_snapshot.xlsx (xlsx, 72KB)]

Key context bullets:
- Pilot: expected 8k tokens/min sustained (chat workloads) for 3 weeks ramp, need low-latency (<120ms p50).
- Prod: phased commit ~6 months, estimate 12-16k tokens/min sustained with burst spikes to 35k tokens/min on marketing events.
- Business ask: minimize upfront reserved slots during pilot, but guarantee a path to headroom for production within 6 weeks.

Thanks — short huddle this week is fine, 30m to align tradeoffs.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Ben —

Wrote a quick sketch of the finance side and attached a cashflow view. High level from finance: pilot should prefer monthly reserved + burst credits vs an annual commit; that gives Acme lower cash outlay and lets us convert if pilot KPIs look good. See included estimates for three scenarios (lean, mid, full).

Quick notes:
- Lean pilot: 2 reserved slots (NVIDIA L40x1 equiv) + 50% burst budget for first 3 weeks.
- Mid pilot: 4 reserved slots + 100% burst.
- Full pilot: 6 reserved slots (higher discount threshold).

I’ll call out expected ARR and cash timing in the spreadsheet. If infra says the lean option is operationally safe (cache + batching tuned), that’s probably the conversation we want to push.

Attachment: [Attachment: acme_pipeline_snapshot.xlsx (updated with finance tab)]

—Laura

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU runway huddle: Acme pipeline & reserve asks

Thanks — quick infra read: the lean pilot (2 reserved) is workable if we do aggressive prefix/KV caching and cap per-tenant concurrency. Operational caveats:

- Cold-start risk: we’ll need warmers for the first 48 hours of pilot windows to avoid p95 spikes.
- Burst capacity: recommend a hot-standby pool (cross-region eligible) rather than pure burst credits; that gives <150ms tail latency during spikes.
- Quantization: for pilot we can run a quantized variant (INT8) to reduce VRAM and increase packing; should validate quality on Acme prompt set.
- SLA: if Sarah wants p50 <120ms, we should tag as "pilot-high-priority" with a canary route and fallbacks.

I attached a short infra scenario doc with recommended reserve->burst mapping and a proposal for a 10% safety margin. From an ops risk perspective, mid pilot is much safer but costs more. If finance wants lean, we’ll need a 24–48 hour ramp plan and two runbooks (normal + emergency scale).

Attachment: [Attachment: runway_scenarios_v2.pdf (pdf, 180KB)]

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acmecorp.com>

Cc: itprocurement@acmecorp.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU runway huddle: Acme pipeline & reserve asks

Thanks Ben & team — helpful context. A couple clarifying Qs from our side before procurement engages formally:

1) Procurement timeline: if we go "lean pilot" (monthly reserved + burst), how quickly can we sign a PO and have capacity available? We need to know procurement lead time to schedule the May 15 start.
2) Data residency & KMS: we will need confirmation on the pilot that logs and KV caches remain within our designated region and that Redwood will accept our KMS for keys used in production.
3) Success criteria: our PM wants a short list of acceptance criteria (latency p50/p95, token throughput, cost per 1k tokens) to approve moving from pilot -> prod.

If you can provide quick answers (1–2 bullets each) we can loop procurement. Happy to hop on a short call.

—Sarah
Sarah Lopez | Head of AI Integrations | Acme Corp

Thanks all — summary & next steps below. I’ll book a 30m alignment tomorrow to finalize mechanics and action owners.

Summary (short):
- Finance (Laura): recommends starting with the Lean pilot (2 reserved monthly + 50% burst) to reduce Acme’s initial cash outlay; mid is fallback.
- Infra (Karthik): lean pilot is possible with warming, aggressive caching, INT8 variant, and a 10% safety margin; recommends a hot-standby pool for spike protection.
- Procurement (Acme): needs procurement lead time + KMS confirmation + explicit success criteria to move forward.

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) Karthik: produce a 1-page ops ramp runbook for the lean pilot (include warmers, canary route, and fallbacks) — ETA Mon 2028-03-19 EOD.
2) Laura: provide the cost delta table (monthly vs annual for pilot tiers) and highlight cashflow implication for ACME — ETA Mon 2028-03-19 noon.
3) Ben: draft the success criteria doc and a short email template for Acme procurement to sign PO quickly — ETA Mon 2028-03-19 EOD.
4) Stephanie: prepare a CS onboarding checklist and 1-week support rota for pilot window — ETA Mon 2028-03-19 EOD.

I’ve attached updated scenario slides that combine finance + infra inputs; will send invite for tomorrow’s 30m.

Attachments: [Attachment: runway_scenarios_v2.pdf, acme_pipeline_snapshot.xlsx]
